== Biography ==

Peter is one of four young rabbits living with their mother in a sand-bank beneath the roots of a great fir-tree. Unlike his siblings—Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail, who are good little bunnies—Peter is very naughty. While his brothers and sisters obey their mother's instruction to gather blackberries down the lane, Peter instead disobeys and runs straight into Mr. McGregor's garden, squeezing beneath the gate.

Once within the garden, Peter eats lettuces, French beans, and radishes in turn. The food makes him feel rather sick, and he sets about looking for parsley. But in searching for relief, he rounds the end of a cucumber frame and comes face to face with Mr. McGregor himself, who is on his hands and knees planting young cabbages.

Mr. McGregor jumps up and gives chase, waving a rake and calling out, 'Stop thief!' Peter is most dreadfully frightened. He rushes all over the garden in panic, for in his terror he has quite forgotten the way back to the gate. The consequence of Peter's naughtiness is now upon him: pursued by an angry farmer through the very garden his mother had warned him never to enter.

== Narrative Role ==

Peter is one of four little rabbits living with their Mother in a sand-bank beneath a great fir-tree. Unlike his siblings Flopsy, Mopsy, and [[Cotton]]-tail—who were good little bunnies—Peter was very naughty. When their mother went out one morning, his siblings dutifully went down the lane to gather blackberries. But Peter, disobedient and mischievous, ran straight away to Mr. [[McGregor]]'s garden and squeezed under the gate.

Once in the garden, Peter indulged himself: he ate lettuces, then French beans, and then radishes in quick succession. The feast soon left him feeling rather sick, and he went to look for parsley. But as he searched near a cucumber frame, he encountered Mr. McGregor himself, who was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages. McGregor jumped up at once and ran after Peter with a rake, calling out "Stop thief!"

Peter was most dreadfully frightened by this sudden turn. He rushed all over the garden in desperate panic, but in his terror he had forgotten the way back to the gate. Presently, Peter sneezed.

== Personality ==

Peter is a rabbit of impulsive and naughty temperament. Where his siblings obey their mother's counsel, Peter acts upon desire without hesitation, willing to transgress into forbidden places. His disobedience speaks to a certain boldness or disregard for warnings—he pursues what attracts him regardless of caution. When real danger presents itself, however, this boldness crumbles into acute fear and disorientation. The contrast between his initial confidence and his later panic reveals a creature whose impulses outpace his judgment, and whose bravery proves fragile when tested by genuine peril.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Cotton]]''' — family. One of Peter's three siblings living with him in the sand-bank.

'''[[Mopsy]]''' — family. One of Peter's three siblings living with him in the sand-bank.

'''[[Rabbit]]''' — family. Peter's mother, who warned him against entering Mr. McGregor's garden and tended to him with camomile tea after his adventure.

'''[[McGregor]]''' — enemy. The farmer who pursued Peter through his garden with a rake, crying "Stop thief!"
